speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start by confirming the details: how many days has the bleeding persisted since your wisdom tooth extraction, and do you notice similar easy bruising on your arms or legs without injury?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: That family history of joint swelling in the uncle is significant; has the patient ever experienced spontaneous bleeding into joints or muscles? REQUEST TEST: PT, PTT, Platelet count.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: PT: 15 sec, PTT: 60 sec, Platelet count: 160,000/mm3

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Previously healthy, takes no medications. Social history: The patient is a high school student with no history of smoking, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, joint pains (except noted in family history), or significant past illnesses. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That previous diagnosis of gastroenteritis does not align with your active gum bleeding and family history of joint issues; can you clarify why the prior doctor suggested that, and have you noticed any blood in your stool or urine? REQUEST TEST: PT, PTT, INR. REQUEST IMAGES: CBC with differential and Peripheral_Smear.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: PT: 15 sec, PTT: 60 sec, INR: Not Provided, CBC with differential: Hematocrit 35%, Leukocyte_Count 8,500/mm3, Platelet_Count 160,000/mm3, Peripheral_Smear: Normal-sized platelets

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A (Factor VIII deficiency)

The prolonged PTT with a normal platelet count and normal bleeding time strongly suggests an intrinsic pathway defect; given the family history of joint swelling and male gender, Hemophilia A is the most likely diagnosis. Does the patient have a known history of hemarthrosis (bleeding into joints) or have any family members with a confirmed Factor VIII deficiency?
